course_info.faculty: Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences

catalog_course_description: This course explores the central issues in contemporary political philosophy such as the nature and value of democracy, freedom, justice, equality, collective well- being, collective identity, and the political institutions these ideals require.
course_learning_outcomes: Identify the main currents of ideas that accompany the various routes to modernity.
Discuss the various manifestations of the main set of ideologies, namely liberalism, conservatism, socialism, anarchism, fascism, nationalism, feminism, and environmentalism.
Compare and contrast these ideologies with each other.
course_objective: To convey the meaning of fundamental, modern political ideologies.

resources: Required Readings eBooks that can be reached online through the Information Center website:
Kevin Harrison and Tony Boyd, Understanding Political Ideas and Movements (Manchester: Manchester University Press, 2003).
Michael Freeden, Ideology: A Very Short Introduction (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2003).
Richard Bellamy and Andrew Mason, Political Concepts (Manchester: Manchester University Press, 2003).
